Here's the MDN-style markdown with the table:

markdown
## Syntax

```js
fetch("http://localhost:7083/api/reservations", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    date: "2026-04-19",
    time: "13:00",
    partySize: 4,
    customerId: "c-126"
  })
});
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `date` | `string` | Yes | Reservation date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. |
| `time` | `string` | Yes | Time in `HH:MM` 24-hour format. |
| `partySize` | `integer` | Yes | Number of guests. Must be a positive integer. |
| `customerId` | `string` | Yes | ID of the customer making the reservation. |

## Return value

Returns a {{jsxref("Promise")}} that resolves with a `201 Created` response containing:

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `id` | `string` | Unique reservation identifier. |
| `status` | `string` | Always `"PENDING"` on creation. |
| `expiresAt` | `string` | ISO 8601 datetime when the reservation expires. |
| `_links.confirm.href` | `string` | Endpoint URL to confirm the reservation. |
| `_links.confirm.method` | `string` | HTTP method for confirmation — always `"POST"`. |

explain this Must be at least 30 minutes in the future.

Apr 25

Claude responded: It means the date + time you send must be at least 30 minutes ahead of the current time when the request is made.

It means the date + time you send must be at least 30 minutes ahead of the current time when the request is made.

For example, if it's currently 13:00, the earliest valid reservation time you can submit is 13:30.

If you send a time that's too soon (or in the past), the API would reject it — typically with a 400 Bad Request and a validation error message like:

json
{
  "error": "validation_error",
  "message": "Reservation time must be at least 30 minutes in the future",
  "field": "time",
  "code": 400
}

This is a common rule in booking systems to give staff enough time to prepare before a customer arrives.

Claude responded: This is a type mismatch error.

This is a type mismatch error. Your save method returns TableReservation but reservationRepository.save() returns TableDefination. They are two different types.

You have two ways to fix it:

Option 1 — Change the return type to match the repository

If reservationRepository works with TableDefination, change the method signature to return TableDefination:

java
@Override
public TableDefination save(TableReservation table) {
    System.out.println("Saving..." + table);
    TableDefination saved = reservationRepository.save(table);
    System.out.println("AFTER SAVE: " + saved);
    return saved;
}

Option 2 — Map TableDefination back to TableReservation

If you must return TableReservation, convert the saved result before returning:

java
@Override
public TableReservation save(TableReservation table) {
    System.out.println("Saving..." + table);
    TableDefination saved = reservationRepository.save(table);
    System.out.println("AFTER SAVE: " + saved);

    // Map back to TableReservation
    TableReservation result = new TableReservation();
    result.setId(saved.getId());
    // copy other fields...
    return result;
}

Root cause — your repository is typed as JpaRepository<TableDefination, ?> but you're passing a TableReservation into it. Check your repository interface:

java
public interface ReservationRepository extends JpaRepository<TableDefination, Long> {
}

If reservations are the core entity, it likely should be:

java
public interface ReservationRepository extends JpaRepository<TableReservation, Long> {
}

Which option fits your structure best?

7:02 PM

Claude responded: The problem is clear.

The problem is clear. You have this line in your repository:

java
TableDefination save(TableDefination table);

Remove it. JpaRepository already provides a save() method typed to TableReservation — you're overriding it with the wrong type, which causes the mismatch throughout your service.

Your repository should look like this:

java
@Repository
public interface TableReservationRepository extends JpaRepository<TableReservation, Long> {

    @Query("SELECT t FROM TableReservation t WHERE t.status = 'AVAILABLE'")
    List<TableReservation> findAvailable();

    List<TableReservation> findByStatus(String status);

    boolean existsByCustomerIdAndReservationDateAndReservationTime(
        String customerId,
        LocalDate reservationDate,
        LocalTime reservationTime
    );
}

Then your service save() will work as-is:

java
@Override
public TableReservation save(TableReservation table) {
    System.out.println("Saving..." + table);
    TableReservation saved = reservationRepository.save(table);
    System.out.println("AFTER SAVE: " + saved);
    return saved;
}

JpaRepository<TableReservation, Long> already gives you save(TableReservation) for free — you never need to declare it manually. The TableDefination line was the only cause of the type mismatch.

Claude responded: The problem is you have two save() methods — one for TableDefination and one for TableReservation — but your repository only works with TableReservation.

The problem is you have two save() methods — one for TableDefination and one for TableReservation — but your repository only works with TableReservation. TableDefination doesn't belong here at all.

Here's the fix across all three files:

1. RestaurantTableRepositoryPort.java — remove TableDefination save

java
public interface RestaurantTableRepositoryPort {
    TableReservation save(TableReservation table);
    List<TableReservation> findAllAvailable();
    List<TableReservation> findByStatus(String status);
    boolean existsByCustomerIdAndDateAndTime(String customerId, LocalDate date, LocalTime time);
}

2. RestaurantTableRepositoryAdapter.java — remove TableDefination save, fix the other

java
@Repository
public class RestaurantTableRepositoryAdapter implements RestaurantTableRepositoryPort {

    private final TableReservationRepository reservationRepository;

    public RestaurantTableRepositoryAdapter(TableReservationRepository reservationRepository) {
        this.reservationRepository = reservationRepository;
    }

    @Override
    public TableReservation save(TableReservation table) {
        System.out.println("Saving..." + table);
        TableReservation saved = reservationRepository.save(table);
        System.out.println("AFTER SAVE: " + saved);
        return saved;
    }

    @Override
    public List<TableReservation> findAllAvailable() {
        return reservationRepository.findAvailable();
    }

    @Override
    public List<TableReservation> findByStatus(String status) {
        return reservationRepository.findByStatus(status);
    }

    @Override
    public boolean existsByCustomerIdAndDateAndTime(String customerId, LocalDate date, LocalTime time) {
        return reservationRepository.existsByCustomerIdAndReservationDateAndReservationTime(customerId, date, time);
    }
}

3. TableReservationRepository.java — no changes needed, already correct

java
@Repository
public interface TableReservationRepository extends JpaRepository<TableReservation, Long> {

    @Query("SELECT t FROM TableReservation t WHERE t.status = 'AVAILABLE'")
    List<TableReservation> findAvailable();

    List<TableReservation> findByStatus(String status);

    boolean existsByCustomerIdAndReservationDateAndReservationTime(
        String customerId,
        LocalDate reservationDate,
        LocalTime reservationTime
    );
}

Root cause summary:

ProblemFix
RestaurantTableRepositoryPort declared save(TableDefination)Removed — only TableReservation is needed
RestaurantTableRepositoryAdapter had two save() methodsKept only save(TableReservation)
reservationRepository.save(table) was receiving TableDefinationNow correctly receives TableReservation

TableDefination should not be passing through the repository layer at all — if you need it elsewhere, it should be mapped from TableReservation at the service layer.

public class TableDefination {

    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    @Column(name = "table_id")
    private String tableId;

    private int capacity;

    private String status;

    public TableDefination() {
        // Required by JPA
    }

    public TableDefination(String tableId, int capacity) {
        this.tableId = tableId;
        this.capacity = capacity;
    }

    public Long getId() {
        return id;
    }

    public String getTableId() {
        return tableId;
    }

    public int getCapacity() {
        return capacity;
    }

    public String getStatus() {
        return status;
    }

    public void setStatus(String status) {
        this.status = status;
    }

    public void setTableId(String tableId) {
        this.tableId = tableId;
    }

    public void setCapacity(int capacity) {
        this.capacity = capacity;
    }

    @Override

        return "TableDefination{id=" + id + ", tableId='" + tableId + "', capacity=" + capacity + ", status='" + status + "'}";

The diagram shows the three concentric hexagonal layers:

  • Domain core (purple) — business logic, entities, use cases. No framework dependencies.
  • Ports (green ring) — interfaces that define how the outside world talks to the domain (driving ports) and how the domain talks to the outside world (driven ports).
  • Adapters (blue ring) — the concrete implementations. Inbound adapters (REST controller, message consumer, GraphQL) drive the app. Outbound adapters (JPA repository, REST client, message publisher) are driven by it.

Click any adapter box to learn more. This matches exactly what your RestaurantTableRepositoryAdapter implements — it's an outbound adapter connecting the domain to JPA.

java
package tableservice.domain;

import jakarta.persistence.*;
import java.time.LocalDate;

@Entity
@Table(name = "table_availability")
public class TableAvailability {

    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    @ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    @JoinColumn(name = "table_id", referencedColumnName = "table_id")
    private TableDefination table;

    private LocalDate startDate;
    private LocalDate endDate;
    private String status;

    // ─── Constructors ───────────────────────────────────────────
    public TableAvailability() {}

    public TableAvailability(TableDefination table, LocalDate startDate, LocalDate endDate, String status) {
        this.table     = table;
        this.startDate = startDate;
        this.endDate   = endDate;
        this.status    = status;
    }

    // ─── Getters ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    public Long getId() {
        return id;
    }

    public TableDefination getTable() {
        return table;
    }

    public String getTableId() {
        return table != null ? table.getTableId() : null;
    }

    public LocalDate getStartDate() {
        return startDate;
    }

    public LocalDate getEndDate() {
        return endDate;
    }

    public String getStatus() {
        return status;
    }

    // ─── Setters ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    public void setTable(TableDefination table) {
        this.table = table;
    }

    public void setStartDate(LocalDate startDate) {
        this.startDate = startDate;
    }

    public void setEndDate(LocalDate endDate) {
        this.endDate = endDate;
    }

    public void setStatus(String status) {
        this.status = status;
    }

    // ─── Utility ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    public boolean isAvailable() {
        return "AVAILABLE".equalsIgnoreCase(this.status);
    }

    public boolean overlaps(LocalDate date) {
        return (date.isEqual(startDate) || date.isAfter(startDate))
            && (date.isEqual(endDate)   || date.isBefore(endDate));
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return "TableAvailability{" +
            "id=" + id +
            ", tableId=" + (table != null ? table.getTableId() : "null") +
            ", startDate=" + startDate +
            ", endDate=" + endDate +
            ", status='" + status + '\'' +
            '}';
    }
}

}

java
package tableservice.domain;

import jakarta.persistence.*;

@Entity
@Table(name = "table_defination")
public class TableDefination {

    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    @Column(name = "table_id", unique = true)
    private String tableId;

    private int capacity;

    private String status;

    @OneToOne(mappedBy = "table", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    private TableAvailability availability;

    // ─── Constructors ───────────────────────────────────────────
    public TableDefination() {}

    public TableDefination(String tableId, int capacity) {
        this.tableId  = tableId;
        this.capacity = capacity;
    }

    public TableDefination(String tableId, int capacity, String status) {
        this.tableId  = tableId;
        this.capacity = capacity;
        this.status   = status;
    }

    // ─── Getters ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    public Long getId() {
        return id;
    }

    public String getTableId() {
        return tableId;
    }

    public int getCapacity() {
        return capacity;
    }

    public String getStatus() {
        return status;
    }

    public TableAvailability getAvailability() {
        return availability;
    }

    // ─── Setters ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    public void setTableId(String tableId) {
        this.tableId = tableId;
    }

    public void setCapacity(int capacity) {
        this.capacity = capacity;
    }

    public void setStatus(String status) {
        this.status = status;
    }

    public void setAvailability(TableAvailability availability) {
        this.availability = availability;
        if (availability != null && availability.getTable() != this) {
            availability.setTable(this);
        }
    }

    // ─── Utility ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    public boolean isAvailable() {
        return availability != null && availability.isAvailable();
    }

    public boolean hasCapacityFor(int partySize) {
        return this.capacity >= partySize;
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return "TableDefination{" +
            "id=" + id +
            ", tableId='" + tableId + '\'' +
            ", capacity=" + capacity +
            ", status='" + status + '\'' +
            '}';
    }
}

Claude responded: You need to create and link a TableAvailability before saving.

You need to create and link a TableAvailability before saving. Here's the fixed method:

java
@PostMapping("/availability")
public ResponseEntity<EntityModel<ReservationResponse>> checkAvailability(
        @RequestBody TableAvailabilityRequest request) {

    System.out.println("Receiving reservation from customer: " + request);
    logger.info("Receiving reservation from customer: {}", request);

    String customerId = request.getCustomerId();
    LocalDate date    = request.getDate();
    LocalTime time    = request.getTime();
    int partySize     = request.getPartySize();

    if (date == null || time == null || customerId == null) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Date, time, and customerId must not be null");
    }

    if (repositoryAdapter.existsByCustomerIdAndDateAndTime(customerId, date, time)) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate reservation detected for this customer, date, and time.");
    }

    LocalDateTime expiresAt = LocalDateTime.of(date, time).plusMinutes(15);

    // 1️⃣ Create and save TableDefination
    TableDefination tableEntity = new TableDefination("tableId123", partySize, "RESERVED");
    TableDefination savedTable  = tableRepositoryAdapter.save(tableEntity);
    System.out.println("Saved TableDefination --> " + savedTable);

    // 2️⃣ Create TableAvailability and link to saved TableDefination
    TableAvailability availability = new TableAvailability(
        savedTable,
        date,
        date,           // endDate = same day for a single reservation
        "UNAVAILABLE"   // mark as unavailable once reserved
    );
    savedTable.setAvailability(availability);

    // 3️⃣ Save availability (cascades from TableDefination automatically)
    TableDefination finalSaved = tableRepositoryAdapter.save(savedTable);
    System.out.println("Saved TableAvailability --> " + finalSaved.getAvailability());

    // 4️⃣ Build response
    ReservationResponse response = new ReservationResponse();
    response.setId(finalSaved.getId());
    response.setStatus("RESERVED");
    response.setExpiresAt(expiresAt);

    EntityModel<ReservationResponse> resource = EntityModel.of(response);
    return ResponseEntity.ok(resource);
}

Here's what changed and why:

StepWhatWhy
Step 1Save TableDefination firstMust have an id before linking to TableAvailability
Step 2Create TableAvailability with savedTableLinks the two via @OneToOne foreign key
Step 3Save TableDefination againCascadeType.ALL auto-saves the linked TableAvailability
Step 4Set status = "RESERVED" in responseWas commented out before

Also make sure TableDefinationRepository has a save() that TableRepositoryAdapter exposes — which it already does from the earlier fix.

Generic hexagonal architecture diagram. The key rules shown:

  • Inbound adapters (blue) — REST, messaging, CLI, scheduler — drive the app through driving ports
  • Driving ports (teal, left) — interfaces the inbound adapters call into
  • Domain core (purple) — pure business logic, zero framework dependencies
  • Driven ports (teal, right) — interfaces the domain calls out through
  • Outbound adapters (coral) — JPA, REST client, queue, cache — implement the driven ports

The golden rule at the bottom: dependencies point inward only — the domain never knows anything outside itself. Click any box to learn more.

partySizeintegerYesNumber of guests. Must be a positive integer. Maximum allowed party size per table is 6. e.g. 4
customerIdstringYesID of the customer making the reservation. e.g. "c-126"

idstringResponseUnique identifier for the reservation. e.g. "2"
statusstringResponseReservation status. Always PENDING on creation.
expiresAtstringResponseISO 8601 expiry datetime. e.g. "2026-04-26T11:15:00"

_links.confirm.methodstringResponseHTTP method for the confirm URL. Always "POST"
